headline_finding.summary: The C8 objective assumed a physics-vs-ML dielectric comparison could be built by porting Onsager onto the same population the shipped mixed-openpoly-radonpy-dielectric-conformal-kpi trains/evaluates on. Testing this surfaced that RadonPy PI1070's 'static_dielectric_const' column -- the ground-truth label for 79% of that KPI's combined population (1077/1372) and the ONLY dielectric-plus-dipole-moment source in this module -- violates a model-independent thermodynamic inequality (eps_static >= eps_infinity = n^2, Frohlich 1949 Ch.2) in 962/1075 = 89.5% of rows. OpenPoly's own internally-consistent DFT decomposition (eps_Total >= eps_Electronic) has ZERO such violations across 295/295 rows, isolating the defect to RadonPy's MD fluctuation-formula route (known in the literature to under-converge for short simulations, especially in weakly-polar polymers). CONSEQUENCE: any physics-vs-ML dielectric comparison scored against this ground truth is comparing a sound physical theory (Onsager) against a majority-corrupted target, not against reality. This does not merely limit the physics arm's accuracy -- it undermines the shipped ML KPI's own training signal for the RadonPy 79% of its population.

DECISIVE_FINDING_data_integrity_audit.interpretation: RadonPy's MD fluctuation-formula static dielectric constant is under-converged for the large majority of (weakly-)polar polymers -- collapsing toward the electronic-only limit or below it -- and cannot serve as ground truth for a physics-vs-ML dielectric comparison as the C8 objective assumed. This is a property of the ground-truth LABELS, not of either predictor; it means the physics-vs-ML-vs-stack numbers below (like the existing shipped ML KPI they are compared to) are being scored against partially-invalid targets on ~90% of the RadonPy population.
DECISIVE_FINDING_data_integrity_audit.observed: 962/1075 = 89.5% of RadonPy static_dielectric_const values VIOLATE this inequality
DECISIVE_FINDING_data_integrity_audit.refute_criterion: eps_static < n_measured^2 for a material is thermodynamically impossible (Frohlich 1949 Ch.2 / Debye 1929: eps(0) >= eps(optical) always, since static permittivity = electronic polarization + non-negative orientational polarization)
